title: Lesion measured at follow-up but not identified at baseline or as a new lesion
intent: Every measurement must belong to a lesion with a known identity and category.
logic: for m in measurements: if m.lesion_id not in lesions: raise finding
msg_review_point: Referential integrity between tumor measurement records and tumor identification records.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: a measurement of {value} mm is recorded for lesion {lesion_id}, but no corresponding lesion identification record exists.
msg_reason: Measurements can only be interpreted against an identified lesion with a category (target/non-target/new) and location. Without it, the lesion cannot enter the sum of diameters, and the derived response may be wrong.
msg_query: A measurement is recorded for lesion {lesion_id} at {visit} but this lesion is not present on the tumor identification form. Please confirm the lesion identification and complete the missing record, or correct the lesion number on the measurement.
msg_tips: Most often a lesion numbering typo, or a new lesion measured before it was formally recorded as new. Check whether the number matches an existing lesion at another site of disease.

title: Duplicate lesion identity
intent: The same anatomical lesion must not be recorded twice.
logic:
group lesions by (subject, organ, laterality, normalised location_detail)
if group size > 1 and both are TARGET or both NON_TARGET: raise finding
msg_review_point: Duplicate recording of the same lesion under two lesion numbers.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesions {lesion_id_a} and {lesion_id_b} are both recorded as {category} at {organ} {laterality} ({location_a} / {location_b}).
msg_reason: If the same lesion is recorded twice, it is counted twice in the sum of diameters, inflating tumor burden and distorting percent change and the nadir.
msg_query: Lesions {lesion_id_a} and {lesion_id_b} appear to describe the same lesion at {organ}. Please confirm whether these are two distinct lesions; if not, please remove the duplicate and update the affected assessments.
msg_tips: Compare the baseline sizes and the size trajectory: identical or near-identical values across visits strongly suggests duplication.

title: Nodal lesion recorded without a short axis
intent: Nodal lesions must be measured in short axis; a longest diameter cannot substitute.
required_fields: CRF specification field semantics (nodal axis source), measurement.axis_recorded where collected
logic:
axis_source = resolve_nodal_axis_source(crf_specification)   # set once at AC-11 intake
   1. explicit axis-type field on the measurement form, if collected
   2. axis implied by the CRF field itself (e.g. a field named 'Short axis (mm)')
   3. protocol default declared at intake

if lesion.is_nodal and axis_source cannot establish the measurement as a short axis:
    raise finding

guards:
  - no finding where the CRF collects a single nodal field whose semantics are unambiguous
  - where axis_source is unresolved for the study, deactivate and report NOT_EVALUATED
msg_review_point: Measurement axis for lymph node lesions.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}, lesion {lesion_id} ({organ} node): the recorded measurement appears to be a longest diameter rather than a short axis.
msg_reason: RECIST 1.1 requires the short axis for nodal lesions, at baseline and at every follow-up. Using the longest diameter overstates the nodal contribution to the sum and can mask a response or create a false progression.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} is a lymph node. Please confirm the measurement recorded at {visit} is the short axis; if the longest diameter was recorded, please correct it.
msg_tips: Nodal lesions were only formally distinguished from RECIST 1.0 onwards in version 1.1; sites experienced with older studies frequently record the long axis out of habit.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 requires nodal lesions to be measured in short axis. The check is on whether short axis can be established, not on whether a particular field was collected.
r1_comment: Some CRF doesn't collect the type of size, instead the CRF directly asks sites to enter size based on the appropriate type. Consider the field name directly mentions right size type, if there's no size type selection field in the CRF.
r1_response: AMENDED. Axis type is now resolved at ingestion in priority order rather than assumed to be a collected field: an explicit axis-type field if one exists, otherwise the axis implied by the CRF field itself as declared in the structured CRF specification, otherwise the protocol default. The rule fires only when no source establishes that a nodal measurement is a short axis.

title: Unit or precision inconsistency
intent: Detect mixed cm/mm entry and implausible precision.
logic:
if original_unit differs within a subject, or a value is < 1 with unit mm,
or a non-nodal target value > 300 mm: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency of measurement units and precision across a subject's records.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: measurements are recorded in {units_seen}; lesion {lesion_id} at {visit} has value {original_value} {original_unit}.
msg_reason: A centimetre value entered in a millimetre field understates a lesion tenfold, which can convert a progression into an apparent response.
msg_query: Please confirm the unit of the measurement for lesion {lesion_id} at {visit} ({original_value} {original_unit}); the value appears inconsistent with the other measurements recorded for this subject.
msg_tips: Check the trajectory of the same lesion across visits — a tenfold step between adjacent visits is diagnostic of a unit error.

title: Assessment visit sequence and date order inconsistent
intent: Visit numbering and assessment dates must be monotonic.
logic: order assessments by visit_number; if assessment_date is not non-decreasing: raise finding
msg_review_point: Chronological consistency of tumor assessment visits.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: {visit_a} ({date_a}) is dated after {visit_b} ({date_b}) although it precedes it in the visit sequence.
msg_reason: Nadir, progression dating and best overall response all depend on chronological order. An out-of-order date can move the nadir and change the progression determination.
msg_query: The assessment dates for {visit_a} and {visit_b} appear inconsistent with the visit sequence. Please verify the assessment dates.
msg_tips: Confirm against the scan dates in the imaging report rather than the visit date, which may reflect the clinic visit rather than the scan.

title: Number of target lesions exceeds the maximum
intent: Target lesion count must not exceed the guideline/protocol maximum.
logic:
n = count(lesions where category == TARGET and identified at baseline)
if n > config.max_target_lesions_total: raise finding
msg_review_point: Maximum number of target lesions permitted at baseline.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} target lesions are recorded at baseline; the maximum permitted is {max_total}.
msg_reason: RECIST {guideline_version} permits a maximum of {max_total} target lesions in total. Additional lesions must be recorded as non-target. Including extra lesions in the sum changes the denominator for percent change and can alter the response category at every subsequent timepoint.
msg_query: {n} target lesions are recorded at baseline for this subject, exceeding the maximum of {max_total} specified in the protocol. Please review the target lesion selection and re-classify the excess lesions as non-target, updating all affected assessments.
msg_tips: Re-selection changes the baseline sum and therefore every subsequent percent change; expect all downstream responses to require re-derivation. Prioritise this issue before reviewing any response mismatch for this subject.

title: Target lesions per organ exceeds the maximum
intent: No more than the permitted number of target lesions may be selected from any one organ.
logic:
for organ, group in targets grouped by organ:
    if count(group) > config.max_target_lesions_per_organ: raise finding
msg_review_point: Maximum number of target lesions per organ.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} target lesions are recorded in {organ}; the maximum permitted per organ is {max_per_organ}.
msg_reason: RECIST {guideline_version} limits target lesions to {max_per_organ} per organ so that the sum represents the overall disease burden rather than one organ. Over-representation of one organ biases the response assessment.
msg_query: {n} target lesions are recorded in {organ}, exceeding the per-organ maximum of {max_per_organ}. Please re-classify the excess lesions as non-target and update the affected assessments.
msg_tips: Lymph nodes in different nodal stations are commonly all coded to a single "lymph node" organ; confirm whether the sponsor's convention treats nodal stations as separate organs before raising.

title: Non-nodal target lesion below the measurability threshold at baseline
intent: Target lesions must be measurable at baseline.
logic:
for t in non-nodal targets:
    threshold = config.min_measurable_non_nodal_mm
    if method == CXR:            threshold = config.min_measurable_cxr_mm
    if method == CLINICAL_EXAM:  threshold = config.min_measurable_clinical_exam_mm
    if baseline value < threshold: raise finding
msg_review_point: Measurability of selected target lesions at baseline.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) measures {value} mm at baseline by {method}, below the {threshold} mm minimum for a measurable lesion.
msg_reason: RECIST {guideline_version} requires a non-nodal lesion to be at least {threshold} mm by {method} to be measurable and therefore eligible as a target lesion. Sub-threshold lesions are subject to unreliable measurement, and including one makes the whole sum unreliable.
msg_query: Target lesion {lesion_id} measures {value} mm at baseline, below the {threshold} mm threshold for measurability by {method}. Please confirm the measurement, or re-classify this lesion as non-target and update the affected assessments.
msg_tips: Check the imaging slice thickness where available: a lesion must be at least twice the slice thickness to be measurable, so a 10 mm lesion on 8 mm slices is not measurable even though it meets the nominal threshold.

title: Nodal target lesion with baseline short axis below 15 mm
intent: Only nodes with short axis at least 15 mm are eligible as target lesions.
logic:
for t in nodal targets:
    if baseline short axis < config.min_measurable_nodal_short_axis_mm: raise finding
msg_review_point: Eligibility of lymph nodes as target lesions (short axis ≥ 15 mm).
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: nodal target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) has a baseline short axis of {value} mm, below the 15 mm requirement.
msg_reason: RECIST 1.1 requires a short axis of at least 15 mm for a node to be measurable and selectable as a target lesion. Nodes with a short axis of 10 to under 15 mm are pathological but non-measurable and should be recorded as non-target; nodes under 10 mm are non-pathological and should not be recorded at all.
msg_query: Nodal target lesion {lesion_id} has a baseline short axis of {value} mm. Please confirm the measurement; a node with short axis below 15 mm should be recorded as a non-target lesion (10 to <15 mm) or not recorded (<10 mm).
msg_tips: This is one of the most frequent baseline errors. Verify that the recorded value is a short axis and not a longest diameter before concluding the selection was wrong.
tests: short axis exactly 15 mm → no finding
short axis 12 mm as target → finding

title: Non-pathological node recorded as a lesion
intent: Nodes with short axis below 10 mm are not pathological and should not be recorded.
logic:
for l in nodal lesions (target or non-target):
    if baseline short axis < config.pathological_node_threshold_mm: raise finding
msg_review_point: Recording of lymph nodes that do not meet the pathological threshold.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: node {lesion_id} ({organ}) has a baseline short axis of {value} mm and is recorded as a {category} lesion.
msg_reason: Under RECIST 1.1 a node with a short axis below 10 mm is considered non-pathological and is not recorded or followed. Recording it adds normal tissue to the disease assessment and can prevent a complete response from being assigned.
msg_query: Node {lesion_id} has a baseline short axis of {value} mm, below the 10 mm pathological threshold. Please confirm whether this node should be recorded as disease; if not, please remove it from the assessment.
msg_tips: Where a node is clinically relevant despite being below threshold (for example biopsy-proven involvement), the site should document the rationale; consider accepting with a comment rather than a data change.

title: Lesion size below twice the imaging slice thickness
intent: Measurability depends on slice thickness, not only on the nominal threshold.
logic: if lesion is target and baseline value < 2 * slice_thickness_mm: raise finding
msg_review_point: Lesion measurability relative to the imaging slice thickness.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} measures {value} mm at baseline on {method} with {slice_thickness} mm slices.
msg_reason: RECIST 1.1 requires a lesion to be at least twice the slice thickness to be measurable; on {slice_thickness} mm slices the minimum measurable lesion is {min_size} mm. Below that, apparent size changes may be partial-volume artefacts rather than real change.
msg_query: Target lesion {lesion_id} measures {value} mm at baseline on images with {slice_thickness} mm slice thickness. Please confirm the lesion is measurable per the imaging manual, or re-classify it as non-target.
msg_tips: Slice thickness often varies between the baseline and follow-up scans; if so, the comparison itself is compromised and merits a note to the imaging vendor.

title: Non-measurable disease type selected as a target lesion
intent: Presentations that are non-measurable by definition must not be target lesions.
logic:
deterministic pre-filter: organ or location text matches a non-measurable pattern
   (ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, leptomeningeal disease,
    lymphangitic lung/skin involvement, inflammatory breast disease,
    simple cyst, blastic bone lesion without soft tissue component,
    abdominal mass identified only by physical examination)
then LLM adjudication over the free text confirms or rejects, returning
   {is_non_measurable: bool, category: string, confidence: 0..1, rationale: string}
raise finding when confirmed; confidence < 0.6 → emit as INFO
msg_review_point: Selection of lesion types that RECIST classifies as non-measurable.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} is described as "{location_detail}" in {organ}, which appears to be {non_measurable_category}.
msg_reason: RECIST classifies {non_measurable_category} as non-measurable disease: it cannot be reproducibly measured in one dimension. Such disease must be recorded as non-target and assessed qualitatively. A non-measurable lesion inside the target sum makes the sum, and every percent change derived from it, unreliable.
msg_query: Target lesion {lesion_id} is described as "{location_detail}". This appears to represent non-measurable disease under RECIST. Please confirm the lesion selection and, if appropriate, re-classify it as a non-target lesion.
msg_tips: Blastic bone lesions are non-measurable, but a lytic or mixed lytic-blastic lesion with an identifiable soft tissue component can be measurable on CT/MRI. Cystic metastases can be measurable, but where non-cystic lesions are available they are preferred as targets.

title: Previously irradiated lesion selected as target without documented progression
intent: Lesions in a previously irradiated field are non-measurable unless progression after radiotherapy is documented.
logic:
if lesion.category == TARGET and (lesion.previously_irradiated or radiotherapy field overlaps lesion site prior to baseline)
   and not documented progression after radiotherapy: raise finding
msg_review_point: Eligibility of lesions within a prior radiotherapy field as target lesions.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) lies in a previously irradiated field (radiotherapy {rt_date}), with no documented progression at that site after treatment.
msg_reason: RECIST treats lesions in a previously irradiated area, or subjected to other locoregional therapy, as non-measurable unless progression of that lesion has been demonstrated since the treatment. Post-radiation change can mimic both response and progression.
msg_query: Target lesion {lesion_id} is located within a prior radiotherapy field. Please confirm whether progression of this lesion has been documented since radiotherapy; if not, the lesion should be recorded as non-target.
msg_tips: Also relevant for lesions treated with ablation, embolisation or surgery during the study — see TE-XD-004 for on-study local therapy.

title: No measurable disease at baseline but target lesions recorded
intent: Consistency between the measurable-disease determination and target lesion recording.
logic:
if reported "measurable disease at baseline" == NO and count(targets) > 0: raise finding
also inverse: if == YES and count(targets) == 0 and measurable lesions exist: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency between the baseline measurable disease flag and the recorded target lesions.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: measurable disease at baseline is recorded as {flag}, but {n} target lesions are recorded.
msg_reason: The measurable-disease determination drives the response algorithm: subjects without measurable disease can only be assigned CR, Non-CR/Non-PD, PD or NE, never PR or SD. An inconsistency here produces a systematically wrong response for every timepoint, and may also affect eligibility.
msg_query: Measurable disease at baseline is recorded as {flag} while {n} target lesions are entered. Please confirm the baseline disease status and correct the inconsistent record.
msg_tips: Check eligibility criteria: if the protocol requires measurable disease, this may also be an eligibility deviation requiring separate escalation.

title: Baseline assessment outside the protocol window relative to first dose
intent: Baseline imaging must be recent enough to represent pre-treatment burden.
logic:
gap = first_dose_date - baseline_assessment_date
if gap > config.baseline_window_days_before_first_dose or gap < 0: raise finding
msg_review_point: Timing of the baseline tumor assessment relative to first dose.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: baseline assessment dated {baseline_date}, first dose {first_dose_date}, a gap of {gap} days against a permitted window of {window} days.
msg_reason: A baseline older than the protocol window may no longer represent the disease burden at the start of treatment, which biases every subsequent percent change. A baseline dated after first dose is not a baseline at all and would understate treatment effect.
msg_query: The baseline tumor assessment ({baseline_date}) falls {gap} days before first dose ({first_dose_date}), outside the protocol window of {window} days. Please confirm the assessment date and whether a protocol deviation has been recorded.
msg_tips: Distinguish the scan date from the assessment or read date; the protocol window normally applies to the scan.

title: Reported baseline sum of diameters does not match the recorded lesions
intent: Arithmetic verification of the baseline sum.
msg_review_point: Recomputation of the baseline sum of diameters from the individual target lesion measurements.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: baseline sum of diameters is reported as {reported} mm; the sum of the {n} recorded target lesions is {derived} mm (difference {difference} mm).
msg_reason: The baseline sum is the reference for every partial response determination. An error of {difference} mm shifts the 30% response threshold and can change the response category at multiple timepoints. Recorded lesions: {lesion_breakdown}.
msg_query: The baseline sum of diameters ({reported} mm) does not equal the sum of the recorded target lesion measurements ({derived} mm). Please verify the individual measurements and the sum.
msg_tips: Check first whether a nodal target was included using its longest diameter, and whether all target lesions have a baseline measurement.
rationale: Verifying a site-entered sum detects transcription error. Verifying a system-derived sum only re-tests the EDC's own arithmetic and would produce noise, so the rule stands down.
r1_comment: In case of the CRF not collecting manual entry for the reported sum, this rule should be ignored. The LLM needs to identify study's CRF capture the information by CRF specification.
r1_response: AMENDED, and this answers SQ-08. Status moves from ACTIVE to CONDITIONAL: the rule requires a site-entered sum field. Whether the sum is site-entered or system-derived is determined from the structured CRF specification at the AC-11 intake, and a derived sum deactivates the rule with an explicit NOT_EVALUATED in the coverage report rather than a silent pass. Applied to TE-FU-001 as well, which carries the identical condition at follow-up.

title: Target lesion selection not favouring the largest measurable lesions
intent: Target lesions should be the largest reproducibly measurable lesions.
logic:
if any non-target measurable lesion at baseline is larger than the smallest target lesion
   by more than config.selection_margin_mm (default 5): raise finding
msg_review_point: Rationality of target lesion selection relative to lesion size.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: non-target lesion {nt_lesion_id} ({nt_value} mm) is larger than target lesion {t_lesion_id} ({t_value} mm).
msg_reason: RECIST directs that target lesions be selected on the basis of size, choosing the largest lesions that are reproducibly measurable, while remaining representative of all involved organs. Selecting smaller lesions as targets while larger measurable lesions are left as non-target reduces the sensitivity of the response assessment.
msg_query: Non-target lesion {nt_lesion_id} ({nt_value} mm) is larger than target lesion {t_lesion_id} ({t_value} mm). Please confirm the target lesion selection rationale, for example poor reproducibility of the larger lesion.
msg_tips: Reproducibility legitimately overrides size — a large but ill-defined or confluent mass is a poor target. Expect a proportion of these to be correctly explained rather than corrected.

title: Target lesion without a baseline measurement
intent: Every target lesion needs a baseline value to enter the sum.
logic: for t in targets: if no baseline measurement with state PRESENT: raise finding
msg_review_point: Completeness of baseline measurements for all selected target lesions.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: target lesion {lesion_id} has no baseline measurement (state recorded as {state}).
msg_reason: Without a baseline value the lesion cannot contribute to the baseline sum, so the reference for percent change is understated and partial response may be reported prematurely.
msg_query: Target lesion {lesion_id} has no baseline measurement. Please enter the baseline measurement, or re-classify the lesion if it was not measurable at baseline.
msg_tips: A target lesion that was not evaluable at baseline should not have been selected as a target; check whether re-selection is required.

title: Assessment method inconsistent between baseline and follow-up for the same lesion
intent: The same lesion should be followed by the same modality throughout.
logic:
for lesion, visits in measurements grouped by lesion:
    if distinct method_at_visit values > 1: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency of imaging modality for each lesion across visits.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} is measured by {method_a} at {visit_a} and by {method_b} at {visit_b}.
msg_reason: RECIST requires the same method of assessment and the same technique at baseline and during follow-up. Different modalities measure different things — a change of modality can produce an apparent size change of the order of the response thresholds without any true biological change.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} was assessed by {method_a} at baseline and {method_b} at {visit_b}. Please confirm the modality used and whether the change was clinically necessary.
msg_tips: Where a modality change was unavoidable, the affected timepoint may need to be treated as not evaluable for that lesion rather than measured.

title: Baseline scans span more days than permitted
intent: All baseline imaging should represent a single point in time.
logic:
span = max(scan_dates) - min(scan_dates)
if span > config.scan_span_max_days: raise finding
msg_review_point: Temporal coherence of the scans composing a single tumor assessment.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: scans span {span} days ({earliest} to {latest}), exceeding the permitted {max_span} days.
msg_reason: An assessment is intended to be a snapshot. When component scans are widely separated, lesions measured on the later scans reflect a different point in the disease course, which distorts the sum and, at baseline, the reference for all later comparisons.
msg_query: The scans comprising the {visit} tumor assessment span {span} days. Please confirm the scan dates and whether all scans belong to this assessment.
msg_tips: Commonly caused by brain MRI scheduled separately from body CT; confirm the imaging manual's tolerance before raising.

title: Lesion location inconsistent with the assigned organ or laterality
intent: Detect coding errors between the free-text location and the coded organ/laterality.
logic:
LLM classifies (organ, laterality, location_detail) as consistent / inconsistent / unclear
with rationale; only "inconsistent" with confidence >= 0.7 raises a finding
msg_review_point: Anatomical consistency between the coded organ, laterality and the free-text lesion description.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} is coded to {organ} {laterality} but described as "{location_detail}".
msg_reason: Organ coding drives the per-organ target lesion limit and the interpretation of new lesions by region. A mismatch can hide a breach of the per-organ limit or misclassify a new lesion.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} is recorded at {organ} {laterality} with the description "{location_detail}". Please confirm the anatomical location and correct the coding if needed.
msg_tips: Laterality errors are the most common subtype and matter most for paired organs (lung, kidney, breast, adnexa).

title: Baseline assessment missing entirely while follow-up assessments exist
intent: No follow-up can be interpreted without a baseline.
logic: if subject has follow-up assessments and no assessment flagged is_baseline: raise finding
msg_review_point: Presence of a baseline tumor assessment for every subject with follow-up data.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} follow-up tumor assessments are recorded but no baseline assessment exists.
msg_reason: Percent change from baseline, the nadir and every response category depend on a baseline. Without it the subject cannot contribute to any efficacy endpoint.
msg_query: No baseline tumor assessment is recorded for this subject although follow-up assessments exist. Please enter the baseline assessment or confirm why it was not performed.
msg_tips: Check whether the baseline was entered under a screening visit name that failed to map; this is frequently a data-transfer issue rather than missing data.

title: Reported sum of diameters does not match the recorded lesions at a follow-up visit
intent: Arithmetic verification of the sum at every timepoint.
msg_review_point: Recomputation of the sum of diameters at each timepoint from the individual target lesion measurements.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: sum of diameters reported as {reported} mm; recomputed from the {n} target lesions as {derived} mm (difference {difference} mm). Lesion contributions: {lesion_breakdown}.
msg_reason: The sum drives percent change from baseline (partial response) and from nadir (progression). A {difference} mm error at this timepoint changes the percent change from {reported_pct}% to {derived_pct}% and the derived response from {reported_response} to {derived_response}.
msg_query: The sum of diameters recorded at {visit} ({reported} mm) does not match the sum of the individual target lesion measurements ({derived} mm). Please verify the individual measurements and the recorded sum.
msg_tips: Check for a lesion measured but omitted from the sum, a lesion recorded as absent but still included, and nodal lesions entered with the wrong axis.
rationale: Same condition as TE-BL-011, applied at follow-up. Amended alongside it for consistency: applying the guard at baseline but not at follow-up would be incoherent.
r1_response: AMENDED alongside TE-BL-011, which carries the identical condition. Accepted at round 1, but the same CRF-dependency applies at follow-up and the pair must move together.

title: Target lesion measurement missing without a not-done reason
intent: Missing data must be explained, not silent.
logic:
if measurement absent or value null and state not in (ABSENT, TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE, NOT_EVALUABLE, NOT_DONE)
   or state in (NOT_EVALUABLE, NOT_DONE) with no reason recorded: raise finding
msg_review_point: Completeness and explanation of missing target lesion measurements.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target lesion {lesion_id} has no measurement and no reason recorded.
msg_reason: An unexplained missing measurement makes the sum incomplete, which forces the target response to not evaluable and can propagate into a missing timepoint for progression-free survival.
msg_query: No measurement is recorded for target lesion {lesion_id} at {visit}. Please enter the measurement or record the reason it could not be assessed.
msg_tips: Distinguish "not evaluable" (lesion could not be assessed) from "absent" (lesion no longer visible); the two have opposite consequences for response.

title: Target response reported despite an unevaluable target lesion
intent: Enforce the not-evaluable rule with its progression exception.
msg_review_point: Handling of not-evaluable target lesions in the timepoint response.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target lesion {lesion_id} is not evaluable, yet the target response is reported as {reported_response}.
msg_reason: When any target lesion cannot be assessed, the sum is incomplete and the true tumor burden is unknown, so the response is not evaluable. The exception is progression: if the measured lesions alone already meet the progression threshold, progressive disease can still be assigned. Here the measured lesions sum to {partial_sum} mm against a nadir of {nadir} mm ({partial_pct}%), which does not reach the progression threshold.
msg_query: Target lesion {lesion_id} is recorded as not evaluable at {visit} while the target lesion response is reported as {reported_response}. Please confirm; where a target lesion cannot be assessed, the target response should normally be not evaluable.
msg_tips: This is a systematic misunderstanding at many sites: a lesion that is "not seen because it resolved" should be recorded as absent, not as not evaluable.

title: Implausible measurement change for a single lesion
intent: Outlier detection on lesion trajectories.
msg_review_point: Plausibility of the change in an individual lesion between consecutive assessments.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} changes from {prev_value} mm at {prev_visit} to {value} mm at {visit} ({pct_delta}% over {interval} days).
msg_reason: A change of this magnitude over {interval} days is unusual and is more often a transcription error, a unit error, or measurement of a different lesion than true biology. The change moves the sum from {prev_sum} mm to {sum} mm and the derived response from {prev_response} to {response}.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} changed from {prev_value} mm to {value} mm between {prev_visit} and {visit}. Please verify the measurement against the imaging report.
msg_tips: Genuine large changes do occur — rapid response to targeted therapy, cavitation, haemorrhage into a lesion, or coalescence of adjacent lesions. Look for a comment or a matching change in a neighbouring lesion.
rationale: No guideline source exists; RECIST 1.1 specifies no plausibility limits on lesion trajectories. The defaults (20 mm absolute, 50% relative, within a 90-day window) are set to catch the common data-entry failures — a decimal shift, a cm/mm confusion, a measurement attributed to the wrong lesion — while staying silent on genuine rapid change, which is clinically real in this population. Thresholds are configuration, to be calibrated on the golden dataset at Step 3 against the observed false-positive rate. Until calibrated, the rule is MINOR with a 0.45 confidence base rate, so it ranks below anything derived from the guideline.
r1_comment: Provide the rationale insisting the proposed threshold. What material or information is referred to make this validation rule.
r1_response: RATIONALE ADDED. These thresholds are not drawn from RECIST — the guideline sets no outlier limits. They are heuristics aimed at transcription error, and they are declared as such rather than dressed up with a citation. Proposed for calibration against the golden dataset at Step 3, where the false-positive rate can actually be measured.

title: Lesion recorded as absent and subsequently measured again
intent: Detect and correctly handle reappearance of a resolved lesion.
msg_review_point: Handling of a target lesion that disappeared and later reappeared.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} was recorded as absent at {absent_visit} and measures {value} mm at {visit}.
msg_reason: A previously resolved target lesion that reappears re-enters the sum of diameters at its measured size; it is not a new lesion, because it was present at baseline. Progression is then judged against the nadir. If it has instead been recorded as a new lesion, progression will be dated incorrectly and the sum will double-count the disease.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} was recorded as absent at {absent_visit} and is measured again at {visit}. Please confirm this is the same baseline target lesion rather than a new lesion, and that it is included in the sum of diameters.
msg_tips: Confirm the protocol's position: some protocols treat reappearance after a complete response as progression in itself. The study configuration setting is reappearance_is_progression = {reappearance_is_progression}.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 does not state whether a target lesion that resolved and later reappears constitutes new-lesion progression, and practice differs. The agent therefore does not assert an answer: ID-01 sets the study convention at intake (default — the lesion re-enters the sum at its measured size and progression is judged by the nadir rule; alternative — reappearance after CR is progression). The rule detects the pattern and checks it was handled consistently with whichever convention the study declared. It escalates only where the site both re-measured the lesion and flagged it as new, which is internally contradictory under either convention.
r1_comment: Provide the rationale insisting the proposed threshold. What material or information is referred to make this validation rule.
r1_response: RATIONALE ADDED. This rule carries no numeric threshold; the parameter in it is the interpretation decision ID-01, which is a protocol question rather than a guideline constant.

title: Inconsistent use of the too-small-to-measure convention
intent: One convention per study.
logic:
if the study contains both TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE states and lesions recorded with the
   default value (e.g. 5 mm) under state PRESENT: raise finding at study level
msg_review_point: Consistency of the convention for lesions that are visible but too small to measure reliably.
msg_issue: Study {study_id}: {n_state} records use the too-small-to-measure state while {n_value} records appear to use a fixed {default} mm value under a present state ({examples}).
msg_reason: The two conventions produce different sums and different eligibility for complete response. Mixing them makes cross-subject comparison unreliable and can make a complete response unassignable for some subjects and assignable for others with identical imaging.
msg_query: Please confirm the convention used for lesions below the limit of reliable measurement at this site, so that the records can be harmonised.
msg_tips: Agree the convention centrally and document it in the imaging manual; retrospective harmonisation is usually preferable to leaving the study mixed.

title: Assessment interval outside the protocol schedule
intent: Assessments must follow the protocol calendar so that progression dating is comparable.
required_fields: protocol_config.assessment_schedule (per visit) or the uniform interval fallback
msg_review_point: Compliance of tumor assessment timing with the protocol-defined schedule and window.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: {interval} days between {prev_visit} ({prev_date}) and {visit} ({date}); the protocol specifies {expected} ± {window} days.
msg_reason: Assessment timing determines the resolution of progression dating and, in randomised trials, the comparability of progression-free survival between arms. Systematically late assessments delay progression detection.
msg_query: The interval between {prev_visit} and {visit} is {interval} days, outside the protocol window of {expected} ± {window} days. Please confirm the assessment date and whether a protocol deviation has been recorded.
msg_tips: Cluster by site: isolated deviations are scheduling reality, but a site with a consistent bias is a monitoring signal.
rationale: Protocols commonly schedule every 6 weeks early and every 12 weeks later, and often widen the window after a defined timepoint. A single interval would raise findings against the protocol's own schedule.
r1_comment: The proposed condition is fine. Since a protocol may define different assessment window for particular assessment timing, consider to get information about study's individual tumor assessment window period.
r1_response: AMENDED. The scalar interval and window are replaced by a per-visit schedule captured at the AC-11 protocol intake, so a protocol that tightens or widens the window at particular timepoints is honoured. The scalar remains as a fallback for protocols with a uniform interval.

title: Missing scheduled assessment before progression or censoring
intent: Detect gaps that affect progression-free survival censoring.
logic:
if gap between assessments >= 2 * config.assessment_interval_days
   and subject still on treatment during the gap: raise finding
msg_review_point: Continuity of tumor assessments while the subject remains on study.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: no tumor assessment between {prev_date} and {date}, a gap of {gap} days spanning approximately {n_missed} scheduled assessments while the subject remained on treatment.
msg_reason: Two or more consecutively missed assessments typically require censoring at the last evaluable assessment in progression-free survival analyses, which reduces the information contributed by this subject and can bias the estimate.
msg_query: No tumor assessment is recorded between {prev_date} and {date} although the subject remained on treatment. Please confirm whether assessments were performed and, if so, enter the data; otherwise please record the reason.
msg_tips: Cross-check against the visit schedule and any unscheduled visits; assessments performed but entered under an unmapped visit name are a common cause.

title: Nodal target lesion recorded as absent or zero
intent: Nodes remain measurable and stay in the sum even when they normalise.
logic:
for each FOLLOW-UP assessment (baseline excluded — a nodal target cannot be absent at
selection, having required a short axis >= 15 mm):
    if lesion.is_nodal and lesion.category == TARGET
       and (state == ABSENT or value == 0)
       and state != TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE:            # ID-02 convention, not an error
           raise finding
msg_review_point: Treatment of nodal target lesions that shrink below the pathological threshold.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: nodal target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}) is recorded as {state_or_zero}.
msg_reason: Under RECIST 1.1 lymph nodes always retain a measurable short axis and are never recorded as absent; they continue to contribute their short axis to the sum even when it falls below 10 mm. The sum therefore need not reach zero for a complete response — what is required is that every pathological node has a short axis below 10 mm. Recording the node as zero understates the sum by its true short axis and can produce a false partial response or complete response.
msg_query: Nodal target lesion {lesion_id} is recorded as {state_or_zero} at {visit}. Lymph nodes should continue to be measured in short axis at every visit, including when they normalise. Please enter the measured short axis.
msg_tips: This is the single most common nodal error and it usually reflects a well-intentioned attempt to make the arithmetic produce a complete response. Explain the rule to the site rather than only requesting the correction.
tests: nodal target with state ABSENT at cycle 4 → finding
nodal target measuring 7 mm short axis → no finding
rationale: RECIST 1.1 keeps nodal target lesions in the sum for the whole study even when they fall below 10 mm and are no longer pathological. Their short axis continues to be recorded; they are never set to absent or zero. Removing a normalised node from the sum understates tumor burden and can manufacture a partial response.
r1_comment: The proposed condition could be applied to follow-up assessment? It's okay to check at baseline's tumor identification, but I'm not sure to check under follow-up assessment.
r1_response: AMENDED, and the scope was the wrong way round. The rule is only meaningful at follow-up: a nodal target cannot be absent at baseline, since it was selected for having a short axis of at least 15 mm. What it catches is a node recorded as absent or zero at follow-up once it has normalised, which drops it out of the sum and produces a falsely low sum and a spurious response. The rule is now explicitly restricted to follow-up, and the too-small-to-measure state is excluded so that ID-02 handling is not flagged as an error.

title: Non-target lesion state missing at a follow-up assessment
intent: Non-target lesions must be assessed qualitatively at every timepoint.
logic: if non-target lesion has no non_target_state at a performed assessment: raise finding
msg_review_point: Completeness of qualitative non-target lesion assessment at each timepoint.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: no assessment is recorded for non-target lesion {lesion_id} ({organ}).
msg_reason: The non-target response contributes to the overall timepoint response, and unequivocal progression of non-target disease is sufficient for progression on its own. A missing non-target assessment leaves the overall response underdetermined.
msg_query: No assessment is recorded for non-target lesion {lesion_id} at {visit}. Please record the status of this lesion.
msg_tips: Sites often assess non-target disease collectively rather than lesion by lesion; check whether the eCRF expects a per-lesion or an overall non-target response.

title: Tumor assessment recorded after death or after the end of study participation
intent: Temporal plausibility against subject-level dates.
logic:
if assessment_date > death_date: raise CRITICAL
if assessment_date > discontinuation_date + config.post_treatment_followup_days: raise MAJOR
msg_review_point: Consistency of tumor assessment dates with subject disposition and vital status.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: tumor assessment dated {date} at {visit}, after the recorded {reference_event} of {reference_date}.
msg_reason: An assessment dated after death or well beyond the end of follow-up indicates an error in one of the two dates. Either error affects analysis: an incorrect assessment date can move the progression date, and an incorrect death date affects survival analysis.
msg_query: The {visit} tumor assessment is dated {date}, after the recorded {reference_event} ({reference_date}). Please verify both dates.
msg_tips: Post-treatment follow-up assessments are legitimate in many protocols; confirm the follow-up period before treating a post-discontinuation assessment as an error.

title: New lesion recorded with an identification date earlier than the visit at which it was first reported
intent: New lesion timing consistency.
logic:
if new lesion identified_at assessment date < the date of the assessment where it first appears
   in measurements: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency between the date a new lesion was identified and the assessment at which it was reported.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: new lesion {lesion_id} is dated {identified_date} but first appears in the assessment data at {visit} ({visit_date}).
msg_reason: The progression date is taken from the first assessment at which the new lesion was observed. An inconsistency between these dates produces the wrong progression date and therefore the wrong progression-free survival time.
msg_query: New lesion {lesion_id} has an identification date of {identified_date} but is first reported at {visit} ({visit_date}). Please confirm the date the lesion was first observed.
msg_tips: Where the lesion was visible in retrospect on an earlier scan, the progression date is normally the earlier scan; this requires a documented radiology decision.

title: Follow-up scans span more days than permitted
intent: Same coherence check as TE-BL-015, applied to follow-up assessments.
logic: span = max(scan_dates) - min(scan_dates); if span > config.scan_span_max_days: raise finding
msg_review_point: Temporal coherence of the scans composing a follow-up assessment.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: component scans span {span} days ({earliest} to {latest}).
msg_reason: Widely separated component scans mean that different parts of the tumor burden are measured at different times, which affects the sum and may affect the progression date.
msg_query: The scans comprising the {visit} assessment span {span} days. Please confirm the scan dates.
msg_tips: Where the span is unavoidable, the assessment date convention (earliest scan or latest scan) should be applied consistently across the study.

title: Identical measurements repeated across three or more consecutive visits
intent: Detect carried-forward values rather than genuine measurement.
logic:
if a lesion has the identical value at >= 3 consecutive assessments
   and the lesion is > config.identical_value_min_mm (default 15): raise finding
msg_review_point: Detection of measurements that may have been carried forward rather than re-measured.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} measures exactly {value} mm at {visits}.
msg_reason: Identical measurements of a lesion of this size across several timepoints are uncommon given normal measurement variability, and may indicate that a previous value was copied rather than the lesion re-measured. If so, the sum does not reflect the current tumor burden.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} is recorded as exactly {value} mm at {visits}. Please confirm that the lesion was measured at each assessment.
msg_tips: Small and stable lesions genuinely produce repeated values; this check is deliberately informational and should be reviewed in the context of the whole subject rather than raised as a query in isolation.

title: Reported target lesion response does not match the derived response
intent: The central check: recompute the target response and compare.
logic:
derived = targetResponse(...)
if reported_target_response != derived and derived is not NOT_APPLICABLE: raise finding
severity CRITICAL when the mismatch changes the overall response, MAJOR otherwise
msg_review_point: Derivation of the target lesion response from the sum of diameters, the baseline sum and the nadir.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target lesion response is reported as {reported} but derives as {derived}. Sum of diameters {sum} mm; baseline {baseline_sum} mm ({pct_baseline}%); nadir {nadir_sum} mm at {nadir_visit} ({pct_nadir}%, absolute change {abs_nadir} mm).
msg_reason: {derivation_explanation}
msg_query: The target lesion response recorded at {visit} is {reported}. Based on the recorded lesion measurements the sum of diameters is {sum} mm, a {pct_baseline}% change from baseline and a {pct_nadir}% change from the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm, which corresponds to {derived}. Please review the recorded response and the underlying measurements.
msg_tips: Before querying the response, confirm the measurements themselves: a response mismatch is frequently a symptom of a measurement or sum error already flagged for this subject. Check the linked findings for this subject first.
tests: nadir 50 mm, current 60 mm (+20%, +10 mm) → PD
nadir 20 mm, current 24 mm (+20%, +4 mm) → SD, not PD
non-nodal all absent, node 8 mm → CR
non-nodal all absent, node 11 mm → PR (not CR)

title: Progression declared on a relative increase without the required absolute increase
intent: Enforce the 5 mm absolute criterion alongside the 20% relative criterion.
logic:
if reported_target_response == PD
   and pct_from_nadir >= config.pd_relative_increase_pct
   and abs_from_nadir_mm < config.pd_absolute_increase_mm: raise finding
msg_review_point: Application of both progression criteria: a relative increase of at least 20% and an absolute increase of at least 5 mm from the nadir.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: progression is reported. The sum increased from a nadir of {nadir_sum} mm to {sum} mm, a {pct_nadir}% increase but only {abs_nadir} mm in absolute terms.
msg_reason: RECIST 1.1 requires both a relative increase of at least {pd_pct}% and an absolute increase of at least {pd_abs} mm from the nadir. The absolute criterion was introduced precisely for small tumor burdens, where a 20% increase can fall within measurement variability. Here the absolute increase of {abs_nadir} mm does not reach {pd_abs} mm, so the derived response is {derived}.
msg_query: Progressive disease is recorded at {visit} based on an increase from the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm to {sum} mm. This is a {pct_nadir}% increase but only {abs_nadir} mm in absolute terms, which does not meet the {pd_abs} mm absolute increase also required by RECIST 1.1. Please review the response assessment, unless progression is based on a new lesion or on unequivocal non-target progression.
msg_tips: Confirm first whether progression was actually driven by a new lesion or by non-target progression, in which case the response is correct and this finding can be rejected. This check applies only to progression driven by the target sum.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 requires both a relative increase of at least 20% from nadir and an absolute increase of at least 5 mm. Applying only the relative criterion is the single most common progression error in collected data, and it deserves its own query text rather than the generic response-mismatch wording. Detection is guaranteed by TE-RS-001; this rule supplies the explanation.
r1_comment:
In order to check both conditions indicating that the reported target response=PD is incorrect, should it have condition as below?
- "if reported_target_response == PD
   and pct_from_nadir < config.pd_relative_increase_pct
   and abs_from_nadir_mm < config.pd_absolute_increase_mm: raise finding".
In addition, the 'TE-RS-002' and 'TE-RS-003' are duplicate with 'TE-RS-001'? If yes, should we keep the two rules in the rule list?
r1_response: KEPT, with the relationship now declared explicitly. On the logic: the proposed variant uses AND, but PD requires both criteria, so 'PD not met' is pct < 20 OR abs < 5 — the AND form is narrower than the correct negation and would miss cases. That complete check already exists as TE-RS-001, which recomputes the response and compares. On duplication: yes, TE-RS-002 and TE-RS-003 are both subsumed by TE-RS-001 for detection. Their value is diagnostic, not detective — TE-RS-001 says the response is wrong, these say why, and the query text differs accordingly. They are now declared as cascade children of TE-RS-001, so when both fire the reviewer sees one finding carrying the specific reason, not two.

title: Progression assessed against baseline rather than against the nadir
intent: Detect the classic error of comparing to baseline when the tumor shrank first.
logic:
if reported_target_response != PD
   and pct_from_nadir >= config.pd_relative_increase_pct
   and abs_from_nadir_mm >= config.pd_absolute_increase_mm:
       raise finding

       # discriminator, not a gate — selects the message and adjusts confidence
       if pct_from_baseline < config.pd_relative_increase_pct:
           variant = COMPARED_AGAINST_BASELINE   # confidence x 1.10
       else:
           variant = PROGRESSION_NOT_APPLIED     # confidence unchanged
msg_review_point: Use of the nadir, rather than baseline, as the reference for progression.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: target response is reported as {reported}. The sum is {sum} mm, which is {pct_baseline}% relative to baseline ({baseline_sum} mm) but {pct_nadir}% relative to the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm recorded at {nadir_visit} — an absolute increase of {abs_nadir} mm.
msg_reason: Progression is assessed against the smallest sum recorded on study, including baseline, not against baseline itself. Because this subject responded before progressing, the comparison against baseline still looks favourable while the comparison against the nadir meets the progression criteria. The derived response is progressive disease.
msg_query: At {visit} the sum of diameters is {sum} mm compared with a nadir of {nadir_sum} mm at {nadir_visit}, a {pct_nadir}% increase of {abs_nadir} mm, which meets the RECIST criteria for progression. The recorded response is {reported}. Please review the response assessment.
msg_tips: This is the most consequential single error class in tumor data: it delays or entirely misses the progression date and directly biases progression-free survival. Always check the nadir visit shown above is itself a complete assessment.
rationale: Removing the third condition widens detection, which is the safer direction. The nadir is the reference for progression under RECIST 1.1, and comparing against baseline after tumor shrinkage is the classic error this rule was written for — but it is not the only way to miss progression, and gating on it let the other ways through.
r1_comment: Question to this rule. Should it consider the pct_from_baseline condition? Given that the proposed condition could check incorrect data well with the 1st and 2nd line (i.e. "if reported_target_response != PD and pct_from_nadir >= pd_pct and abs_from_nadir_mm >= pd_abs"), if 3rd line condition isn't definitely deciding data consistency, I suggest to have rule conditions without 3rd line condition.
r1_response: AMENDED as suggested. The baseline comparison is removed from the gate, so the rule now catches every case where progression criteria are met from nadir but progression was not reported. The baseline comparison is retained purely as a discriminator: where percent change from baseline also falls short of the threshold, the site almost certainly compared against baseline instead of nadir, and the finding carries that specific wording and a higher confidence. Where it does not, the finding is still raised with generic wording.

title: Complete response reported while measurable disease persists
intent: Enforce the full complete response definition, including nodal short axis.
logic:
if reported_target_response == CR and (
      any non-nodal target with state != ABSENT
   or any nodal target with short axis >= config.pathological_node_threshold_mm
   or any target with state in (TOO_SMALL_TO_MEASURE, NOT_EVALUABLE)): raise finding
msg_review_point: Conditions required for a complete response of target lesions.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: complete response is reported for target lesions, but {blocking_description} (lesion {lesion_id}: {value} mm, state {state}).
msg_reason: A complete response of target lesions requires the disappearance of all non-nodal target lesions and a reduction of every pathological lymph node, whether target or non-target, to a short axis below {node_threshold} mm. A lesion that is still visible, including one recorded as too small to measure, is not a disappearance.
msg_query: A complete response is recorded at {visit}, but {blocking_description}. Please review the response assessment and the individual lesion records.
msg_tips: Note the asymmetry that causes most of these: the sum of diameters can be very small without a complete response being appropriate, because nodes retain a short axis. Conversely, complete response does not require the sum to be zero.

title: Reported non-target response does not match the derived response
intent: Recompute the non-target response and compare.
logic:
derived = nonTargetResponse(...)
if reported_non_target_response != derived: raise finding
msg_review_point: Derivation of the non-target lesion response from the individual non-target lesion states.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: non-target response is reported as {reported} but derives as {derived}. Lesion states: {non_target_breakdown}.
msg_reason: {derivation_explanation}
msg_query: The non-target lesion response recorded at {visit} is {reported}, while the individual non-target lesion assessments ({non_target_breakdown}) correspond to {derived}. Please review.
msg_tips: A complete response of non-target disease additionally requires every pathological lymph node to be below 10 mm short axis, and where the protocol uses tumor markers, normalisation of those markers.

title: Non-target complete response reported while a pathological node persists
intent: Nodal condition for non-target complete response.
logic:
if reported_non_target_response == CR
   and any non-target node with short axis >= config.pathological_node_threshold_mm: raise finding
msg_review_point: Nodal condition for a complete response of non-target disease.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: non-target complete response is reported while node {lesion_id} ({organ}) measures {value} mm short axis.
msg_reason: A complete response requires all lymph nodes, target and non-target alike, to have reduced to a short axis below {node_threshold} mm. A node of {value} mm remains pathological, so the non-target response is Non-CR/Non-PD.
msg_query: A complete response of non-target lesions is recorded at {visit}, but node {lesion_id} measures {value} mm in short axis. Please review the non-target response.
msg_tips: Non-target nodes are often not measured at all; where the eCRF does not capture a short axis for non-target nodes, this check depends on the radiology narrative and may need to be raised as a clarification rather than a correction.

title: Unequivocal non-target progression reported in a subject with responding or stable measurable disease
intent: Apply the guideline's "exceptional circumstance" test.
logic:
if non_target_response == PD and target_response in (CR, PR, SD) and new_lesion != YES:
    raise finding
    LLM assesses the recorded non-target descriptions for evidence of substantial overall
    worsening; strong evidence downgrades to INFO
msg_review_point: Threshold for declaring unequivocal progression of non-target disease when measurable disease is present.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: unequivocal progression of non-target disease is reported while the target lesion response is {target_response} (sum {sum} mm, {pct_nadir}% from nadir) and no new lesion is recorded. Non-target findings: {non_target_breakdown}.
msg_reason: RECIST states that where measurable disease is present, unequivocal progression based on non-target disease alone should be an exceptional circumstance: the increase in overall tumor burden must be comparable in magnitude to the increase that would be required to declare progression for measurable disease. A modest increase in one non-target lesion is not sufficient, particularly while the target lesions are {target_response}.
msg_query: Unequivocal progression of non-target disease is recorded at {visit} while the target lesions show {target_response}. Please confirm that the overall tumor burden has increased substantially, and provide the radiological description supporting unequivocal progression.
msg_tips: Genuine cases exist — for example a marked increase in a pleural effusion or in lymphangitic disease. The question to the site is not "is this wrong" but "what supports unequivocal". Where the answer supports it, accept and record the rationale so the same finding is not re-raised.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 treats unequivocal non-target progression in the presence of responding or stable measurable disease as an exceptional circumstance requiring substantial worsening of overall tumor burden. That judgement rests on the images and the investigator's overall impression, neither of which is in the collected data. Raising it as a site query invites a defensive answer; raising it to the study team invites a look at the images.
r1_comment: This isn't decisive with entered data only. Check whether it could downgrade the severity to 'INFO'.
r1_response: AMENDED to INFO. You are right that collected data cannot settle this — the guideline's test is a judgement about overall tumor burden that the recorded non-target states do not capture. Note the consequence, which is intended: INFO findings do not enter the default query worklist, so this becomes a study-team observation rather than a site query. The adjudicator can still escalate to MAJOR where the recorded descriptions actively contradict the reported progression.

title: Reported overall response does not match the RECIST overall response table
intent: The overall response must follow from its three components.
logic:
derived = overallTimepointResponse(reported_target, reported_non_target,
                                   reported_new, has_measurable)
if reported_overall != derived:
    finding.expected_driver = the component that determines derived
                              (target / non-target / new lesion)

    if a finding from TE-RS-001, TE-RS-005 or TE-RS-009 is open for this assessment:
        attach as a cascade child of that finding; do not raise a separate query
    else:
        raise finding, naming expected_driver and the component values used

note: computed from the REPORTED components, so this rule isolates table-application
      errors from measurement errors, which are covered by TE-RS-001 and TE-RS-005
msg_review_point: Application of the RECIST overall response table to the reported target, non-target and new lesion components.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: overall response is reported as {reported_overall}, while the recorded components (target {target}, non-target {non_target}, new lesion {new_lesion}) correspond to {derived_overall}.
msg_reason: {table_explanation}
msg_query: The overall response recorded at {visit} is {reported_overall}. Based on the recorded components — target lesion response {target}, non-target response {non_target}, new lesions {new_lesion} — the overall response should be {derived_overall}. Please review.
msg_tips: The combinations most often mis-applied are: target complete response with persisting non-target disease, which is a partial response rather than a complete response; and any new lesion, which is progression regardless of the target and non-target results.
tests: target CR, non-target Non-CR/Non-PD, no new → PR
target PR, non-target CR, new lesion YES → PD
target NE, non-target Non-CR/Non-PD, no new → NE
rationale: The rule derives the overall response from the REPORTED components, which isolates a table-application error from a measurement error. That isolation is only useful if the two are not queried twice — hence the cascade.
r1_comment: Is it possible to give information whether any issue in the individual response (target, non-target) and their relevant detail data (e.g. tumor size, individual lesion response) in order not to avoid duplicate query in both sides (i.e. overall response, target/non-target response)
r1_response: AMENDED. The rule now declares its component dependencies, and the cascade grouping suppresses the separate overall-response query whenever a component finding is already open for the same assessment. Where no component finding exists, the overall-response finding is raised alone and names which component drove the expected value, so the site receives one query identifying the specific field rather than two queries about the same visit.

title: New lesion flag inconsistent with recorded new lesions
intent: Cross-check the flag against the lesion records.
logic:
if new_lesion_flag == YES and no lesion with category NEW at this assessment: raise finding
if new_lesion_flag == NO  and a lesion with category NEW is first recorded here: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency between the new lesion indicator and the recorded new lesion identifications.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: the new lesion indicator is {flag} while {lesion_situation}.
msg_reason: A new lesion is sufficient for progression on its own. If the indicator and the lesion records disagree, either progression has been declared without a documented lesion, or a documented new lesion has not been reflected in the response — both change the progression date.
msg_query: The new lesion indicator at {visit} is recorded as {flag} while {lesion_situation}. Please reconcile the new lesion records with the response assessment.
msg_tips: Check whether the lesion was recorded as a new lesion at a later visit than the one where it was first seen; the progression date follows the first observation.

title: New lesion recorded but overall response is not progression
intent: A confirmed new lesion always means progression under RECIST 1.1.
logic:
if new_lesion_flag == YES and reported_overall != PD: raise finding
   (under iRECIST the expected value is iUPD; see TE-IR-001)
msg_review_point: Effect of an unequivocal new lesion on the overall timepoint response.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: an unequivocal new lesion is recorded ({new_lesion_description}) but the overall response is reported as {reported_overall}.
msg_reason: Under RECIST 1.1 the appearance of any unequivocal new lesion is progression, irrespective of the target and non-target responses. {irecist_note}
msg_query: A new lesion is recorded at {visit} while the overall response is {reported_overall}. Please confirm the new lesion and review the overall response assessment.
msg_tips: Where the finding is equivocal rather than unequivocal, the correct handling is to record it as equivocal and continue treatment, treating the timepoint as not evaluable and re-assessing at the next visit; if later confirmed, progression is dated to this visit.
rationale: Retired at the Step 2 review as fully subsumed by TE-RS-008 (overall response versus the component table), TE-RS-009 (flag versus recorded lesions) and TE-IR-001 (iUPD under iRECIST).
r1_comment:
Check if this rule is duplicate, considering TE-RS-008.
If duplicate rule, I suggest remove this rule, instead, add only iRECIST condition to the TE-RS-008.
r1_response: RETIRED — you are right. TE-RS-008 derives the overall response from the reported components, and the new-lesion flag is one of those components, so a recorded new lesion with a non-PD overall response already fires TE-RS-008. The one case that is not covered — a new lesion present in the lesion table while the flag says NO — is TE-RS-009. The iRECIST expectation needs no folding in, because TE-IR-001 already requires iUPD rather than PD where iRECIST applies. The id is retained permanently and never reused, so historical findings stay interpretable.

title: New lesion in an anatomical region not imaged at baseline
intent: Ensure the region-not-imaged case was considered explicitly.
required_fields: imaging_metadata.regions_imaged (or inferred from baseline lesion organs and modality)
logic: if new lesion organ/region was not covered by the baseline imaging: raise finding
msg_review_point: Interpretation of a lesion found in a region that was not imaged at baseline.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: a new lesion is recorded in {organ}, a region that does not appear to have been imaged at baseline ({baseline_regions}).
msg_reason: A lesion identified in a region that was not scanned at baseline is considered a new lesion, and therefore progression, because pre-existing disease at that site cannot be excluded. The point of this check is to confirm that the site made this determination deliberately rather than by default, since the alternative interpretation — that the lesion was present but unimaged — is not permitted.
msg_query: A new lesion is recorded in {organ} at {visit}. Baseline imaging does not appear to have covered this region. Please confirm the finding represents a new lesion and that baseline imaging of this region was not performed.
msg_tips: Brain metastases are the usual case: many protocols do not require baseline brain imaging, so a first brain scan performed for symptoms yields lesions that must be treated as new. Confirm the protocol's imaging requirements before raising.
rationale: Rejected at the Step 2 review. The premise does not hold: investigator-discretion imaging routinely covers regions absent from the baseline protocol imaging, so region coverage is not evidence of a data problem.
r1_comment: New lesion could be confirmed by other organ/region not covered by the baseline image, because of doing other image by investigator's discretion. Suggest not to run this rule.
r1_response: RETIRED as rejected. Imaging performed at investigator discretion outside the baseline coverage is routine and entirely legitimate, and a new lesion found that way is a real new lesion. The rule assumed baseline coverage bounded where disease could be found, which is not how imaging is actually ordered. The id is retained permanently and never reused.

title: New lesion based on FDG-PET without confirmatory anatomical imaging
intent: Apply the PET rules for new lesion determination.
logic:
if new lesion method == PET and no corresponding CT/MRI finding at the same site
   and no negative baseline PET recorded: raise finding
msg_review_point: Use of FDG-PET to establish a new lesion.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: a new lesion in {organ} is based on FDG-PET, without a corresponding finding on anatomical imaging and without a negative baseline PET.
msg_reason: A positive FDG-PET finding establishes a new lesion when the baseline PET was negative, or when the new site is confirmed on CT or MRI. Without either, a positive PET alone is not sufficient, because the finding may represent disease present but not FDG-avid or not imaged at baseline, or may be non-malignant uptake.
msg_query: The new lesion recorded at {visit} in {organ} is based on FDG-PET. Please confirm whether a baseline PET was performed and negative, or whether the lesion is confirmed on CT or MRI.
msg_tips: Inflammatory and infectious uptake is common, particularly under immunotherapy; anatomical confirmation matters most in that setting.

title: Equivocal new lesion later confirmed but progression not back-dated
intent: Progression is dated to the first observation of a lesion later confirmed.
logic:
if a lesion was EQUIVOCAL at visit i and confirmed unequivocal at visit j > i:

    # guard — progression established at visit j on its own terms
    if at visit j the target criteria for PD are met from nadir
       or non-target response at visit j is PD independently of this lesion:
           no finding: visit j is the correct progression date

    elif the recorded progression date != date of visit i:
           raise finding
msg_review_point: Dating of progression when an equivocal finding is subsequently confirmed.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: lesion {lesion_id} was recorded as equivocal at {first_visit} ({first_date}) and confirmed at {confirm_visit} ({confirm_date}); the progression date is recorded as {recorded_pd_date}.
msg_reason: Where therapy continues after an equivocal finding and the finding is subsequently confirmed as a new lesion, progression is dated to the time of the initial observation, not to the confirming assessment. Using the later date overstates progression-free survival by {days_difference} days.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} was equivocal at {first_visit} and confirmed at {confirm_visit}. Please confirm the date of progression; per RECIST the progression date should be the date of the initial observation ({first_date}).
msg_tips: Under iRECIST the handling differs — the iUPD and iCPD dates are both retained and the analysis convention is protocol-specific. Check which criteria govern before applying this rule.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 dates progression to the first observation of a lesion subsequently confirmed as new. That provision governs only when the new lesion is the progression driver. Applying it where progression arose independently at the later visit would wrongly move the date earlier and shorten PFS.
r1_comment: This rule should consider the case that the visit j's data has definitive rationale of PD. E.g. At the visit j, there is evidence to determine PD due to other conditions (e.g. target lesion sum mm passes 20% worsen and over minimum increase)
r1_response: AMENDED. A guard now suppresses the finding where progression at visit j is independently established by the target or non-target criteria. Back-dating is only correct where the equivocal-then-confirmed lesion is what drove progression; where the target sum crossed the threshold at visit j in its own right, visit j is the correct progression date and the earlier equivocal observation is irrelevant to it.

title: Complete or partial response counted as best overall response without confirmation
intent: Enforce the protocol's confirmation requirement.
logic:
if config.response_confirmation_required
   and reported_best_overall_response in (CR, PR)
   and no subsequent assessment >= config.confirmation_min_interval_days later
      with a response of at least the same rank: raise finding
msg_review_point: Confirmation of complete and partial responses where the protocol requires it.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: best overall response is recorded as {reported_bor} based on {first_visit} ({first_date}), but the next assessment {next_description} does not confirm it.
msg_reason: The protocol requires confirmation of a complete or partial response by a repeat assessment performed no less than {confirm_days} days after the criteria were first met. Without confirmation the response is unconfirmed and the derived best overall response is {derived_bor}. Counting unconfirmed responses inflates the objective response rate.
msg_query: The best overall response is recorded as {reported_bor} based on the assessment at {first_visit}. A confirmatory assessment at least {confirm_days} days later does not appear to support this response. Please review the best overall response.
msg_tips: Check whether a confirmatory scan exists but was entered as an unscheduled visit; also check the interval, since a confirmation performed too early does not satisfy the requirement.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 (Eisenhauer 2009, section on confirmatory measurement) requires that in non-randomised trials where response is the primary endpoint, a complete or partial response be confirmed by a repeat assessment performed no less than 4 weeks after the criteria for response are first met. The default confirmation_min_interval_days is therefore 28. The rule is CONDITIONAL on the protocol requiring confirmation at all — randomised trials with a time-to-event primary endpoint commonly do not — and the interval is protocol configuration confirmed at the AC-11 intake, not a hard-coded constant.
r1_comment: Provide the rationale insisting the proposed threshold. What material or information is referred to make this validation rule.
r1_response: RATIONALE ADDED, and this one does have a guideline source, unlike TE-FU-004.

title: Reported best overall response does not match the derived best overall response
intent: Recompute best overall response across the whole subject timeline.
logic:
derived = bestOverallResponse(orderedTimepoints, config)
if reported_bor != derived.bor: raise finding
msg_review_point: Derivation of best overall response across all timepoints, applying the confirmation requirement and excluding assessments after progression.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: best overall response is reported as {reported_bor}; derived as {derived_bor}. Timepoint responses considered: {timepoint_sequence}.
msg_reason: {bor_explanation}
msg_query: The best overall response recorded for this subject is {reported_bor}. Based on the recorded timepoint responses ({timepoint_sequence}) and the protocol's confirmation requirement, the best overall response derives as {derived_bor}. Please review.
msg_tips: Two frequent causes: a response recorded after progression being counted, and a stable disease result assigned before the protocol's minimum duration from baseline has elapsed.

title: Partial response or stable disease assigned to a subject without measurable disease at baseline
intent: Non-target-only subjects have a restricted response vocabulary.
logic:
if subject has no target lesions at baseline
   and reported_overall in (PR, SD): raise finding
msg_review_point: Permitted response categories for subjects with non-measurable disease only.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: overall response is reported as {reported_overall}, but no target lesions were selected at baseline.
msg_reason: A subject with non-measurable disease only can be assigned a complete response, Non-CR/Non-PD, progressive disease or not evaluable. Partial response and stable disease require measurable disease, since both are defined by a change in the sum of diameters. The corresponding category here is Non-CR/Non-PD.
msg_query: The overall response at {visit} is recorded as {reported_overall} although no target lesions were identified at baseline. Please review; for subjects with non-measurable disease only, the appropriate categories are complete response, Non-CR/Non-PD, progressive disease or not evaluable.
msg_tips: Check first whether target lesions were in fact selected but failed to load — a missing target lesion record produces this finding spuriously. Look for a companion structural finding on this subject.

title: Stable disease assigned before the protocol's minimum duration
intent: Stable disease requires a minimum interval from baseline.
logic:
if reported_overall == SD
   and (assessment_date - baseline_date) < config.sd_min_duration_days: raise finding
msg_review_point: Minimum duration from baseline required before stable disease can be assigned.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: stable disease is reported {days} days after baseline; the protocol requires a minimum of {min_days} days.
