msg_reason: Stable disease is meaningful only if maintained for a minimum interval defined by the protocol. An earlier assessment cannot establish stability, and counting it inflates the disease control rate.
msg_query: Stable disease is recorded at {visit}, {days} days after baseline, which is shorter than the minimum of {min_days} days specified in the protocol. Please review the response assessment.
msg_tips: This affects best overall response rather than the timepoint response in many conventions; confirm the sponsor's derivation convention before querying the site.

title: Response recorded after a documented progression
intent: Post-progression assessments must not contribute to response endpoints.
logic:
if an assessment after the first PD carries a response in (CR, PR, SD)
   and it contributes to the reported best overall response: raise finding
msg_review_point: Treatment of assessments performed after progression in response derivation.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: progression is recorded at {pd_visit} ({pd_date}), and a response of {response} is recorded at {later_visit} ({later_date}).
msg_reason: Best overall response is determined from the assessments recorded from the start of treatment until progression. Assessments after progression are retained in the data but do not contribute to the response endpoints. Including one here changes the best overall response from {derived_bor} to {reported_bor}.
msg_query: A response of {response} is recorded at {later_visit}, after progression was recorded at {pd_visit}. Please confirm the progression date and the response assessments.
msg_tips: Where the subject continued treatment beyond progression, the later assessments are legitimate data; the issue is their use in derivation, not their existence. If iRECIST applies, progression may have been unconfirmed and the later assessments are then fully valid — check the applicable criteria.

title: Recorded progression date does not match the earliest assessment meeting progression criteria
intent: Progression dating.
logic:
derived_date = progressionDate(orderedTimepoints, config)
if |reported_progression_date - derived_date| > 0 days: raise finding
msg_review_point: Dating of disease progression relative to the assessments that meet progression criteria.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: progression date recorded as {reported_date}; the earliest assessment meeting progression criteria is {derived_visit} on {derived_date} ({days_difference} days difference).
msg_reason: Progression-free survival is measured to the date of the first assessment demonstrating progression. A difference of {days_difference} days changes the event time for this subject and, aggregated across subjects, biases the survival estimate.
msg_query: The progression date is recorded as {reported_date}, while the earliest assessment meeting progression criteria is {derived_visit} on {derived_date}. Please confirm the date of progression.
msg_tips: Distinguish radiological progression from clinical progression: if progression was determined clinically, the date may legitimately precede any imaging, and the record should say so.

title: Investigator and independent central review assessments discordant
intent: Surface discordance where both streams exist.
msg_review_point: Concordance between the investigator assessment and the independent central review.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: investigator response {inv_response}, central review response {bicr_response}. {date_note}
msg_reason: Discordance between the investigator and central review is expected at some rate, but discordance that crosses a progression boundary affects the primary endpoint where the central review is the basis of analysis, and may indicate a systematic difference in lesion selection or measurement at this site.
msg_query: Not applicable: this finding is for internal review and reconciliation and is not normally issued as a site query.
msg_tips: Review the lesion-level data from both readers side by side. Consistent directional discordance at one site is a monitoring signal; scattered discordance is normal reader variability. Where the sponsor keeps the two streams deliberately separated, this rule should be disabled in configuration.

title: RECIST 1.1 progression not recorded as unconfirmed progression under iRECIST
intent: First progression under iRECIST is iUPD, never iCPD.
logic:
if guideline includes iRECIST and RECIST 1.1 criteria for PD are met at this timepoint
   and no prior iUPD exists
   and reported irecist_response != iUPD: raise finding
msg_review_point: Assignment of unconfirmed progression when RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are first met under iRECIST.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are met ({pd_driver_description}) and the iRECIST response is recorded as {reported_irecist}, with no preceding unconfirmed progression.
msg_reason: Under iRECIST, the first timepoint at which RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are met is assigned unconfirmed progression (iUPD). Confirmed progression (iCPD) can only be assigned at a subsequent assessment that demonstrates further worsening. Recording confirmed progression at first occurrence removes the confirmation step that iRECIST exists to provide, and may lead to treatment being discontinued for pseudoprogression.
msg_query: RECIST 1.1 progression criteria are met at {visit} and the iRECIST response is recorded as {reported_irecist}. Under iRECIST the first occurrence of progression should be recorded as unconfirmed progression (iUPD), with confirmation at the next assessment. Please review.
msg_tips: The commonest cause is the site applying RECIST 1.1 habits to an iRECIST study. Where both RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST responses are collected, the RECIST 1.1 field correctly reads PD while the iRECIST field should read iUPD — the two are not in conflict.

title: Confirmatory assessment after unconfirmed progression missing or outside the window
intent: iUPD must be followed by a confirmatory assessment within the protocol window.
msg_review_point: Timing of the confirmatory assessment following unconfirmed progression.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: unconfirmed progression recorded at {iupd_visit} ({iupd_date}); {confirmation_situation}.
msg_reason: iRECIST requires the confirmatory assessment between {window_min} and {window_max} days after unconfirmed progression. Assessing too early risks confirming transient pseudoprogression as true progression; assessing too late leaves the subject on a potentially ineffective therapy and leaves the progression date ambiguous. Without a confirmatory assessment, progression remains unconfirmed and the subject's progression status for analysis is indeterminate.
msg_query: Unconfirmed progression was recorded at {iupd_visit} on {iupd_date}. {confirmation_situation}. Please confirm whether a confirmatory tumor assessment was performed and enter the data, or record the reason it was not performed.
msg_tips: Where the subject discontinued treatment at unconfirmed progression, no confirmation is expected and this finding should be rejected with that reason; check the disposition data before querying.

title: Confirmed progression assigned without meeting the confirmation criteria
intent: iCPD requires further worsening in the category that drove iUPD.
logic:
if reported_irecist == iCPD:
    verify per driver recorded at the preceding iUPD:
      TARGET     -> sum >= iUPD.sum + config.icpd_target_increment_mm
      NON_TARGET -> further unequivocal worsening recorded
      NEW_LESION -> new lesion sum >= iUPD.new_lesion_sum + config.icpd_new_lesion_increment_mm
                    or additional new lesions
      or a new driver now independently meets RECIST 1.1 progression criteria
    if none satisfied: raise finding
msg_review_point: Criteria for confirming progression under iRECIST.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: confirmed progression is recorded. Unconfirmed progression was driven by {driver} at {iupd_visit}; at this assessment {confirmation_evidence}.
msg_reason: Confirmation of progression requires further worsening in the category that drove the unconfirmed progression: an increase of at least {target_increment} mm in the target lesion sum relative to the unconfirmed progression timepoint, further unequivocal worsening of non-target disease, an increase of at least {new_increment} mm in the sum of new measurable lesions, or the appearance of additional new lesions. A new category independently meeting RECIST 1.1 progression criteria also confirms. None of these is evident here, so the response should remain unconfirmed progression or reset according to the current burden.
msg_query: Confirmed progression is recorded at {visit}. The unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit} was driven by {driver}, and the current assessment shows {confirmation_evidence}. Please review the confirmation of progression against the iRECIST criteria.
msg_tips: Note the reference point: confirmation compares against the unconfirmed progression timepoint, not against the nadir. This differs from RECIST 1.1 and is a frequent source of confusion.

title: New lesion measurements added to the baseline target sum
intent: iRECIST tracks new lesions separately.
logic:
if reported_sum at a timepoint equals derived baseline-target sum + new lesion measurements
   (within tolerance) rather than the baseline-target sum alone: raise finding
msg_review_point: Separate recording of new lesion measurements from the baseline target lesion sum under iRECIST.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: the reported sum of {reported} mm matches the baseline target sum ({target_sum} mm) plus the new lesion measurements ({new_sum} mm) rather than the target sum alone.
msg_reason: Under iRECIST, new lesions are recorded and measured separately from the baseline target lesions, with their own sum of up to five new measurable lesions, two per organ. They are never added to the baseline target sum, because the baseline sum must remain comparable to baseline for response assessment, while the new lesion sum is used to judge confirmation of progression. Combining them corrupts both.
msg_query: The sum of diameters at {visit} appears to include the measurements of new lesions. Under iRECIST new lesions are recorded and summed separately from the baseline target lesions. Please review the sum of diameters and the new lesion records.
msg_tips: Confirm the eCRF design supports separate new lesion recording; where it does not, this is a study set-up issue affecting every iRECIST subject rather than a site error.

title: Response reset after unconfirmed progression not applied correctly
intent: When progression is not confirmed, the response returns to iCR/iPR/iSD against the original nadir.
msg_review_point: Reassignment of response when progression is not confirmed at the next assessment.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit} was not confirmed, and the response is recorded as {reported_irecist}; the derived response is {derived_irecist} (sum {sum} mm against the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm at {nadir_visit}).
msg_reason: If confirmation criteria are not met, the subject's response resets to iCR, iPR or iSD according to the current tumor burden measured against the original nadir. The nadir is not reset by the unconfirmed progression, so a later increase can again produce unconfirmed progression. This is the mechanism by which iRECIST accommodates pseudoprogression.
msg_query: Unconfirmed progression was recorded at {iupd_visit} and was not confirmed at {visit}. The response at {visit} is recorded as {reported_irecist}; based on the current sum of {sum} mm against the nadir of {nadir_sum} mm the response derives as {derived_irecist}. Please review.
msg_tips: Multiple episodes of unconfirmed progression are permitted and are not an error. What is not permitted is treating the unconfirmed progression sum as the new reference.

title: New measurable lesions exceed the iRECIST limits
intent: At most five new measurable lesions, two per organ.
logic:
if count(new measurable lesions) > config.max_new_target_lesions_total
   or count per organ > config.max_new_target_lesions_per_organ: raise finding
msg_review_point: Limits on the number of new measurable lesions recorded and measured under iRECIST.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: {n} new measurable lesions are recorded ({per_organ_breakdown}); iRECIST permits up to {max_total} in total and {max_per_organ} per organ.
msg_reason: The new lesion sum is used to judge confirmation of progression, so it must be constructed consistently. Additional new lesions beyond the limits are recorded as new non-target lesions rather than measured.
msg_query: {n} new measurable lesions are recorded for this subject. iRECIST permits up to {max_total} new measurable lesions in total, and {max_per_organ} per organ, with any further new lesions recorded as non-target. Please review the new lesion records.
msg_tips: The appearance of numerous new lesions is itself strong evidence of true progression, so this finding is usually a recording issue rather than a clinical question.

title: Assessments continue after confirmed progression without documented rationale
intent: iCPD is terminal for response derivation.
logic:
if assessments exist after an iCPD timepoint and are assigned iRECIST responses
   other than iCPD: raise finding
msg_review_point: Handling of assessments performed after confirmed progression.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: confirmed progression recorded at {icpd_visit} ({icpd_date}); subsequent assessments at {later_visits} carry responses of {later_responses}.
msg_reason: Confirmed progression is the terminal response state. Later assessments may be collected for follow-up, but assigning a non-progression response after confirmed progression is inconsistent and risks the later response being carried into the best overall response derivation.
msg_query: Assessments after the confirmed progression at {icpd_visit} carry responses of {later_responses}. Please confirm the progression status and the response assessments recorded after it.
msg_tips: Check whether the earlier assessment was in fact unconfirmed rather than confirmed progression; a mislabelled iCPD is the more likely error.

title: Treatment continued beyond unconfirmed progression without documented clinical stability
intent: iRECIST permits continuation only for clinically stable subjects.
required_fields: cross_domain.exposure, cross_domain.performance_status or clinical stability assessment
logic:
if treatment continued after an iUPD
   and no record of the clinical stability assessment exists at that timepoint: raise finding
msg_review_point: Documentation of clinical stability when treatment continues beyond unconfirmed progression.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: treatment continued after unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit}, with no recorded assessment of clinical stability.
msg_reason: iRECIST permits treatment beyond unconfirmed progression only where the subject is clinically stable: no decline in performance status, no worsening of symptoms attributable to disease, and no need for intensified management. The documentation supports both subject safety and the interpretation of the subsequent assessment.
msg_query: Treatment continued after unconfirmed progression at {iupd_visit}. Please confirm that the subject was assessed as clinically stable at that time and that this is documented.
msg_tips: This is a protocol compliance point as much as a data point; where the eCRF has no field for it, escalate to the monitoring team rather than issuing a data query.

title: RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST responses collected in parallel are mutually inconsistent
intent: Where both are collected, the iRECIST value must follow from the RECIST 1.1 value and the state history.
logic:
expected = irecistStateMachine(...) applied to the reported RECIST 1.1 responses
if reported_irecist != expected: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency between the parallel RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST response assessments.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: RECIST 1.1 response {r11_response}, iRECIST response {reported_irecist}; the iRECIST response derived from the RECIST 1.1 sequence is {expected_irecist}.
msg_reason: The iRECIST assessment is derived from the same underlying measurements as the RECIST 1.1 assessment, differing only in the treatment of progression and new lesions. Given the RECIST 1.1 result at this timepoint and the preceding response history, the iRECIST response should be {expected_irecist}.
msg_query: The RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST responses recorded at {visit} are {r11_response} and {reported_irecist}. Based on the response history the iRECIST response would be expected to be {expected_irecist}. Please review.
msg_tips: Where the two fields are on separate forms completed by different people, expect systematic divergence at a site; treat that as a training signal rather than a per-record query.

title: Study uses immunotherapy but responses are assessed under RECIST 1.1 only
intent: Detect a study-level configuration mismatch.
logic:
if protocol specifies iRECIST and no iRECIST responses are present in the data,
   or the reverse: raise study-level finding
msg_review_point: Alignment between the response criteria specified in the protocol and the response data collected.
msg_issue: Study {study_id}: the protocol specifies {configured_guideline}, but {observed_situation}.
msg_reason: If iRECIST is specified but not collected, pseudoprogression cannot be distinguished from true progression, and subjects may be discontinued prematurely. If iRECIST is collected but not specified in the protocol, the analysis convention is undefined. Either way the endpoint derivation is at risk across the whole study.
msg_query: Not applicable: this is a study set-up finding for the study team rather than a site query.
msg_tips: Raise with the study data manager and the biostatistician; resolution usually requires a database change rather than data correction.

title: End of treatment due to progression but no progression recorded in the tumor data
logic:
if disposition reason indicates progressive disease
   and no assessment with overall response PD (or iCPD) exists: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency between the reason for treatment discontinuation and the recorded tumor response.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: treatment discontinued on {disposition_date} for {disposition_reason}, but no assessment records progressive disease. Last recorded response: {last_response} at {last_visit}.
msg_reason: If treatment stopped for progression, either an assessment demonstrating progression is missing from the tumor data, or the discontinuation reason is incorrect. Both affect the progression-free survival analysis: a missing progression event leads to censoring instead of an event.
msg_query: Treatment was discontinued for {disposition_reason} on {disposition_date}, but no tumor assessment recording progression is present. Please confirm whether a tumor assessment demonstrating progression was performed, and enter the data if so; if progression was determined clinically, please confirm the basis and the date.
msg_tips: Clinical progression without radiological confirmation is legitimate and common near end of life; the record should show it as such rather than leaving the tumor data silent.

title: Progression recorded in the tumor data but treatment continued without documented rationale
msg_review_point: Continuation of study treatment after documented progression.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: progression recorded at {pd_visit} ({pd_date}); study treatment continued until {last_dose_date}, {days} days beyond progression.
msg_reason: Treatment beyond progression may be permitted by the protocol, but it must be documented, and it changes the interpretation of subsequent assessments. Where it is not permitted, this is a protocol deviation. Where the study uses iRECIST, the earlier assessment may have been unconfirmed progression rather than confirmed progression, in which case continuation is expected and the response coding needs review instead.
msg_query: Study treatment continued for {days} days after the progression recorded at {pd_visit}. Please confirm the progression assessment and whether continuation beyond progression was approved.
msg_tips: Check the applicable response criteria first — under iRECIST this pattern is normal and the finding should be rejected.

title: New anticancer therapy started before recorded progression
logic:
if a new systemic anticancer therapy starts before the recorded progression date
   (or before any recorded progression): raise finding
msg_review_point: Timing of new anticancer therapy relative to the recorded progression.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: new anticancer therapy ({therapy}) started on {therapy_date}; recorded progression date {pd_date_or_none}.
msg_reason: Starting a new anticancer therapy before recorded progression usually indicates that progression occurred but was not captured, or that treatment changed for another documented reason. In progression-free survival analyses the start of new therapy is commonly a censoring or event-defining event, so the discrepancy has direct analytical consequences, and any tumor assessment after the new therapy no longer reflects the study treatment.
msg_query: A new anticancer therapy ({therapy}) started on {therapy_date}, before any recorded disease progression. Please confirm the reason for starting new therapy and whether a tumor assessment demonstrating progression was performed.
msg_tips: Radiotherapy for symptom palliation is a frequent benign explanation; distinguish it from a change of systemic therapy.

title: Local therapy applied to a target lesion during the study
logic:
if radiotherapy, surgery or ablation is recorded at a site matching a target lesion
   after baseline: raise finding on all subsequent assessments of that lesion
msg_review_point: Effect of locoregional therapy on the interpretation of a target lesion.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: {procedure} was applied to {site} on {procedure_date}, matching target lesion {lesion_id}; measurements of this lesion continue at {later_visits}.
msg_reason: Once a lesion has received locoregional therapy, its subsequent size no longer reflects the systemic treatment effect, and RECIST treats such lesions as non-measurable unless progression is demonstrated. Continuing to include it in the sum understates tumor burden and can produce a spurious partial response.
msg_query: {procedure} was applied to {site} on {procedure_date}, which corresponds to target lesion {lesion_id}. Please confirm and clarify how this lesion has been assessed at subsequent visits.
msg_tips: The usual analytical convention is that the subject is considered to have progressed, or is censored, at the time of local therapy to a target lesion; confirm the protocol's convention with the statistician.

title: Adverse event indicating disease progression without a corresponding tumor assessment
logic:
if an AE term maps to disease progression / malignant neoplasm progression
   and no PD assessment exists within config.ae_pd_window_days (default 60): raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency between adverse events indicating disease progression and the tumor assessment data.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: adverse event "{ae_term}" with onset {ae_date}; no tumor assessment recording progression within {window} days.
msg_reason: An adverse event of disease progression implies a clinical determination of progression. If the tumor data does not reflect it, the progression event may be missing from the efficacy analysis, or the adverse event may have been coded inappropriately — disease progression is frequently reported as an adverse event when it should be captured as an efficacy outcome.
msg_query: An adverse event of "{ae_term}" is recorded with onset {ae_date}. Please confirm whether disease progression was documented and whether a tumor assessment was performed at that time.
msg_tips: Many sponsors instruct sites not to report disease progression as an adverse event; where that convention applies, the finding is also a coding issue for the safety team.

title: Death recorded before the last tumor assessment or before the progression date
logic: if death_date < last assessment_date or death_date < recorded progression date: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency of the death date with the tumor assessment and progression dates.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: death recorded on {death_date}; {conflicting_record} dated {conflict_date}.
msg_reason: A tumor assessment or progression date after the date of death is impossible, so one of the dates is wrong. Both feed survival and progression-free survival analyses directly.
msg_query: The date of death ({death_date}) precedes {conflicting_record} ({conflict_date}). Please verify both dates.
msg_tips: Partial dates are a frequent cause; check whether an imputed date is being compared against a complete one.

title: Tumor marker not normalised while a complete response is reported
logic: if reported overall response == CR and marker value > upper limit of normal: raise finding
msg_review_point: Normalisation of tumor markers as a condition of complete response, where the protocol requires it.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: complete response reported while {marker} is {value} {unit} (upper limit of normal {uln}).
msg_reason: Where the protocol includes tumor markers in the response definition, a complete response requires marker normalisation in addition to the disappearance of all lesions. A persistently elevated marker means the response is Non-CR/Non-PD.
msg_query: A complete response is recorded at {visit} while {marker} remains above the upper limit of normal ({value} {unit}). Please review the response assessment.
msg_tips: Marker elevation can have non-malignant causes; the site's explanation may be sufficient without a data change.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 states that where tumour markers are initially above the upper limit of normal, they must normalise for a subject to be considered in complete response, alongside the disappearance of all lesions. The comparator is the reporting laboratory's ULN carried on the lab record, so no threshold is invented here. The rule is CONDITIONAL on the protocol declaring that markers contribute to the CR determination, since many solid-tumor protocols collect markers without giving them a role in response.
r1_comment: Provide the rationale insisting the proposed threshold. What material or information is referred to make this validation rule.
r1_response: RATIONALE ADDED. The threshold is the laboratory's own upper limit of normal, not a value the agent chooses.

title: Imaging modality not among those permitted by the protocol
logic: if measurement method not in config.allowed_modalities: raise finding
msg_review_point: Use of imaging modalities permitted by the protocol and imaging charter.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: lesion {lesion_id} assessed by {method}; the protocol permits {allowed_modalities}.
msg_reason: Modalities differ in sensitivity and in measurement reproducibility. Using a modality outside the protocol makes the measurement non-comparable with the rest of the subject's data and with other subjects.
msg_query: Lesion {lesion_id} was assessed by {method} at {visit}, which is not among the modalities specified in the protocol. Please confirm the modality used.
msg_tips: Contrast versus non-contrast CT is the most consequential variant and is often not captured as a distinct modality; consider whether the eCRF should distinguish them.

title: Required disease-site imaging missing
logic:
if the protocol requires imaging of a region (e.g. brain in a study enrolling subjects
   with brain metastases) and no assessment covers that region: raise finding
msg_review_point: Coverage of all protocol-required anatomical regions at each assessment.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: no assessment of {required_region} although the protocol requires it{subject_context}.
msg_reason: Disease in an unimaged region cannot be assessed, and a lesion later found there must be treated as a new lesion. Missing required imaging therefore both reduces the reliability of the current response and risks a spurious progression later.
msg_query: No assessment of {required_region} is recorded at {visit} although the protocol requires it. Please confirm whether the imaging was performed and enter the results.
msg_tips: Brain imaging is the usual case, particularly in lung cancer and melanoma studies.

title: Best overall response inconsistent with the subject's timepoint responses at study level
logic: if reported_bor rank is better than the best reported timepoint response: raise finding
msg_review_point: Consistency of the recorded best overall response with the recorded timepoint responses.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: best overall response recorded as {reported_bor}, while the best timepoint response recorded is {best_timepoint} at {visit}.
msg_reason: The best overall response cannot be better than any response actually recorded at a timepoint. This indicates either a missing timepoint assessment or an incorrect best overall response.
msg_query: The best overall response is recorded as {reported_bor}, but the best response recorded at any timepoint is {best_timepoint}. Please review.
msg_tips: Check for an unscheduled assessment that was not entered; a response confirmed at an unscheduled visit is a common cause.

title: Subject has no post-baseline assessment
logic:
if subject has a baseline assessment, received treatment,
   and has no post-baseline tumor assessment: raise finding
msg_review_point: Availability of at least one post-baseline tumor assessment for each treated subject.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: treated from {first_dose_date} with no post-baseline tumor assessment; last known status {status}.
msg_reason: A treated subject with no post-baseline assessment is not evaluable for response and is censored at randomisation or treatment start in progression-free survival, which reduces the power of the analysis. The reason should be documented.
msg_query: No post-baseline tumor assessment is recorded for this subject. Please confirm whether an assessment was performed, and record the reason if it was not.
msg_tips: Early death or early withdrawal are the usual explanations and are legitimate; the finding exists to ensure the reason is captured.

title: Site-level pattern of the same finding
logic:
if a rule fires for >= config.site_pattern_min_subjects (default 3) subjects at one site
   and the site's rate exceeds the study rate by config.site_pattern_factor (default 3):
   raise one aggregate finding and link the individual findings
msg_review_point: Detection of systematic issues at a site rather than isolated data errors.
msg_issue: Site {site_id}: rule {source_rule_id} ({source_rule_title}) fires for {n_subjects} of {site_subjects} subjects, against a study rate of {study_rate}%.
msg_reason: A concentration of the same issue at one site usually reflects a training or process gap rather than isolated errors. Addressing it at the site level resolves the whole cluster and prevents recurrence, whereas issuing individual queries treats the symptom.
msg_query: Not applicable: this finding is directed to the monitoring team rather than to the site as a data query.
msg_tips: Pair with a site training action and re-check at the next data cut; the recurrence status on the linked findings will show whether the intervention worked.

title: Finding already covered by an open query
logic: classification produced by the query reconciler; see queryReconciliation
msg_review_point: Suppression of findings already covered by an outstanding query.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: finding {source_finding_id} is already covered by open query {query_id} raised on {opened_date}.
msg_reason: Re-issuing a query that is already outstanding creates duplicate work at the site and confuses the audit trail. The finding is retained and linked, but is suppressed from the default worklist until the query is answered.
msg_query: Not applicable: no new query is required.
msg_tips: If the outstanding query is materially different in scope from this finding, disposition the finding as NEW manually and issue a distinct query.

title: Query answered or closed but the answer does not justify the current data
intent: Assess whether the site's answer to an earlier query reasonably explains the current data. Escalate only where it does not.
msg_review_point: Whether an answered or closed query actually resolved the underlying data issue, or reasonably justified leaving the data as it is.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: query {query_id} was {query_status} on {resolution_date} with the answer "{answer_summary}", but the data still shows {current_state}.
msg_reason: The query was resolved without the data being corrected. The site's answer does not explain why the current values are correct, so the issue survives into the locked database. Where an answer does justify the data, this finding is suppressed instead and the justification is recorded against the record.
msg_query: Query {query_id} regarding {issue_summary} was answered on {resolution_date}, but the data still shows {current_state}. Please clarify: if the data is correct as entered, please explain the basis; otherwise please make the correction.
msg_tips: Read the original answer in full before re-querying — it is quoted above. Where the site confirmed the data is correct and the explanation holds, disposition this as justified so it is not raised again at the next data cut.

title: Issue recurs after a previous resolution
logic:
if a finding with this dedupe key was RESOLVED in an earlier run
   and evaluates true again in the current run: mark RECURRENT and escalate
msg_review_point: Recurrence of a previously resolved issue.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: this issue was resolved on {previous_resolution_date} (run {previous_run_id}) and is present again in the current data.
msg_reason: A recurrence usually means either that a data correction was reverted, or that a subsequent data entry reintroduced the same error. Both are worth understanding, because the same cause is likely to affect other records.
msg_query: This issue was previously raised and resolved on {previous_resolution_date}, and is present again in the current data. Please confirm the current value and clarify the reason for the change.
msg_tips: Compare the audit trail of the affected field across the two data cuts; a reverted correction and a fresh error need different responses.

title: Critical query outstanding beyond the ageing threshold
logic:
if a query linked to a CRITICAL finding is OPEN for > config.query_aging_days (default 30):
   raise finding
msg_review_point: Ageing of outstanding queries linked to endpoint-critical findings.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: query {query_id} concerning {issue_summary} has been open for {days} days.
msg_reason: Endpoint-critical data cannot be locked while the query is outstanding, and late resolution compresses the timeline before database lock. Ageing queries on response data are a leading cause of lock delay.
msg_query: Not applicable: this finding is for the study team's query management rather than a new site query.
msg_tips: Escalate through the monitoring team rather than by reissuing the query.

title: Query answer does not address the question asked
logic:
LLM classifies the answer against the query as
   {addresses: full | partial | none, intent: data_will_be_corrected | data_confirmed_correct |
    clarification_provided | unrelated, confidence}
raise when addresses == none or partial with confidence >= 0.7
msg_review_point: Responsiveness of query answers to the question asked.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}: query {query_id} asked "{query_summary}"; the answer "{answer_summary}" appears to {addresses_description}.
msg_reason: An unresponsive answer that is nonetheless accepted closes the query without resolving the underlying data question, so the issue survives into the locked database.
msg_query: Thank you for the response to query {query_id}. The original question concerned {query_summary}; could you please also confirm {outstanding_point}?
msg_tips: Site answers are often correct but terse. Read the original answer in full before re-querying; the model flags candidates rather than making the determination.

title: Data changed after a query but a new inconsistency was introduced
logic:
if a data value changed between runs in response to a query
   and a NEW finding with a different rule id now exists on the same record: link and raise
msg_review_point: Verification that data corrections did not introduce new inconsistencies.
msg_issue: Subject {subject_id}, {visit}: {field} was changed from {old_value} to {new_value} following query {query_id}; the record now triggers {new_rule_id} ({new_rule_title}).
msg_reason: Corrections made in isolation frequently break a dependent value — most often a lesion measurement corrected without the sum or the response being updated. The correction should be applied consistently across the dependent fields.
msg_query: Following the correction to {field} at {visit}, {new_issue_summary}. Please review the related fields so the assessment is internally consistent.
msg_tips: This is why measurement corrections should always be reviewed together with the sum and the response for the same timepoint, and for all later timepoints if the nadir moved.

title: New or worsening effusion used as evidence of progression without cytological confirmation
intent: Progression driven by an effusion must rest on cytological confirmation where the measurable disease is responding or stable.
required_fields: reported_responses.overall, non_target_state, lesion description text, derived target response, cytology result where collected
logic:
for each assessment a where reported overall response == PD:
    effusions = non-target or new-lesion records at a whose organ or description
                matches an effusion pattern (pleural, pericardial, peritoneal / ascites)
    for e in effusions:
        appeared  = e not present at the previous assessment
        worsened  = e.non_target_state moved toward worsening since the previous assessment
        if (appeared or worsened)
           and derived target_response at a in (CR, PR, SD)
           and no cytology or histology result recorded for e:
               raise finding

guards:
  - suppress when unequivocal progression is evidenced independently of the effusion
  - suppress when derived target response is itself PD
  - deactivate when the protocol waives cytological confirmation (set at AC-11 intake)
  - deactivate when no cytology field is collected, reporting NOT_EVALUATED
msg_review_point: Whether a new or worsening effusion used to support progression carries the cytological confirmation RECIST requires.
msg_issue: Progressive disease is recorded at {visit} for subject {subject_id}. The supporting non-target finding is {effusion_description}, which {appeared_or_worsened} at this visit, while target lesions show {target_response_derived}. No cytological result is recorded for the effusion.
msg_reason: RECIST 1.1 requires that an effusion appearing or worsening during treatment be confirmed cytologically before it is taken as evidence of progression, where the measurable disease is responding or stable. Effusions arise from causes unrelated to tumor progression, including the treatment itself and intercurrent illness. An unconfirmed effusion is a recognised source of spurious progression, which censors the subject early and shortens progression-free survival.
msg_query: Progressive disease is recorded at {visit}, supported by {effusion_description}, while target lesions show {target_response_derived}. Please confirm whether cytological assessment of the effusion was performed and record the result. If cytology was not performed, please confirm the basis on which progression was assessed.
msg_tips: This matters most where the effusion is the sole basis for progression; where other unequivocal progression exists the finding is suppressed. Some protocols explicitly waive cytological confirmation — check the protocol before querying, and if it is waived, deactivate this rule at the AC-11 intake rather than dispositioning each occurrence.
rationale: RECIST 1.1 requires cytological confirmation of an effusion appearing or worsening on treatment before it is taken as progression, where the measurable disease is responding or stable.
